passage: At the community centre's holiday camp, the art room was buzzing. Bidisha's two older cousins, Lakshmi and Rohan, had set up a board game at the big table and were laughing over private jokes. Bidisha stood by the door holding her paintbrush. Her throat felt tight. She walked over and asked, "Can I play too?" Rohan said the game was for two. She said, "Maybe we can start a new round with three?" Lakshmi shrugged, but Rohan still said no. Bidisha did not argue. She joined her friend Meena at the clay table and later told the camp helper what had happened, in a calm voice.

qa.q: What were Lakshmi and Rohan doing at the big table?
qa.a: They had set up a board game and were laughing over private jokes.

qa.q: What might Bidisha have been feeling when she stood by the door holding her paintbrush?
qa.a: She probably felt left out and hurt, and her tight throat shows the sting of being excluded.

qa.q: What could Bidisha try if the cousins keep leaving her out tomorrow?
qa.a: She could suggest a different game, keep playing with Meena, and, if it keeps happening, tell the camp helper or a family elder calmly, as she did.

qa.q: How might Lakshmi have seen the moment?
qa.a: Lakshmi may have gone along with Rohan without thinking much about Bidisha; the shrug suggests Lakshmi was unsure or did not want to disagree with Rohan.

grounding: A child is left out by two older cousins, asks to join, finds another friend, and calmly tells an adult.

passage: Every summer at Nani's house in Lucknow, my older cousins Amandeep and Farah shut themselves in the back room with their card games. I'm Imran, the youngest by three years, and I used to stand outside the door listening to them laugh. That summer I tried something new. I knocked and said, 'Can I play? I learnt rummy.' Farah said, tossing her plait, 'You'll slow us down.' It stung. I tried again. 'What if we play something for three, like ludo?' Amandeep shrugged, but Farah shut the door. So I went to the courtyard and played marbles with my little cousin Zaid, which was actually fun. At dinner I told Nani, calmly, 'They never let me in.' Nani didn't fuss. The next day she set up a family carrom match and put me on Amandeep's team.

qa.q: What game did Imran suggest for three?
How did Imran feel when Farah said 'You'll slow us down'?
qa.a: Stung and left out, after trying hard to join.

qa.q: Which steps did Imran try, and which worked?
qa.a: Asking to join and suggesting a game for three didn't work; playing with Zaid and calmly telling Nani did, and Nani set up a family carrom match.

qa.q: Why might Farah want to keep the room to herself?
qa.a: She may enjoy time with a cousin her own age and see Imran as too young, without noticing how it hurts.

grounding: A child left out by two older cousins asks to join, suggests a game, plays with another cousin and calmly tells a grandparent.

passage:
Note to Didi, from Sangeeta Mami, after the mehendi night.
I wanted you to know how Pallavi handled the evening. Kavita and Juhi, the older cousins, spent the whole night whispering and practising their own dance, and turned their backs whenever Pallavi came near. I watched her try. She asked, 'Can I learn the steps?' They said, 'Later.' She suggested all three of them play musical chairs. No. Her lip wobbled. Then she found little Manav by the henna table, and they made up a silly dance together. Near midnight she came to me and said quietly, 'Kavita and Juhi keep leaving me out.' No tears, no drama. I thanked her for telling me and spoke to the girls. Kavita taught her the steps before breakfast.

qa.q: Who did Pallavi dance with by the henna table?
What did Pallavi's wobbling lip show?
qa.a: She felt hurt and left out after asking twice and being turned away.

qa.q: How did Pallavi handle being excluded?
qa.a: She asked to join, suggested a game, played with Manav, and calmly told Mami, who spoke to the older girls.

qa.q: How might Kavita see the evening?
qa.a: Mostly as fun with Juhi, perhaps not noticing how left out Pallavi felt until Mami spoke to her.

grounding: An aunt's note describes a girl left out by older cousins at a family function who tries to join, plays with a younger cousin and calmly tells an adult.
